triggerReason: Federated identity and release state were durable, but operators could not follow degradation through one time-series, deduplicated incident, audited notification and temporary-access lifecycle.
action: Added workspace-scoped SLO samples and hour/day traceability, alert and incident state machines, signed webhook retry/dead-letter/receipt handling, suppression and escalation, delegated access reviews, dual-approved break-glass, deployment-controller contract conformance, and an accessible Operations Center.
outcome: NEXUS-7 can now explain when operational health changed, which raw evidence caused an incident, who was notified, whether temporary authority expired, and whether an external deployment adapter survives deterministic fault injection.
evidence: 744 hourly raw SLO samples aggregate into 744 hour and 31 day buckets with exact raw-ID traceability
Repeated matching alerts reuse one incident and preserve every causal occurrence
Signed webhook delivery is idempotent, retries with bounded backoff, records receipts, and exposes dead letters
Maintenance windows, explicit suppressions, storm budgets and delayed escalation have deterministic failure paths
Access review can auto-revoke overdue authority and break-glass disappears after its short TTL
Reference deployment-controller chaos covers timeout, retry, duplicate, partial payload, telemetry ordering and rollback
Operations Center passes bilingual component, desktop browser, mobile and WCAG A/AA checks
Memory and real PostgreSQL repositories, migrations, checksum backup and restore remain compatible with v1.0-v1.3 data
119 standard tests, 6 real PostgreSQL tests, 14 browser/axe tests, 12 model cases, a production build and 10,000-tick stress run pass
